name: VA TURP versus watchful waiting
question: Does immediate transurethral resection reduce treatment failure compared with watchful waiting in men with moderate BPH symptoms?

arms.label: Immediate transurethral resection of the prostate

design.population: 556 men aged 55 years or older with a 10–20/27 symptom score and moderate BPH symptoms.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Selection of Patients and Assignment to Treatment, pp 75–76; Results, Screening, p 76

verdictNote: Watchful-waiting crossover to surgery reached 65/276 (24%) by three years.
takeaway: Among 556 men with moderate BPH symptoms, immediate TURP reduced three-year composite treatment failure versus watchful waiting (23/280 [8.2%] versus 47/276 [17.0%]; RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30–0.77; P = 0.002 for event rates).

reports.label: Three-year primary report
reports.citation: Wasson JH, Reda DJ, Bruskewitz RC, et al. "A Comparison of Transurethral Surgery with Watchful Waiting for Moderate Symptoms of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *N Engl J Med.* 1995;332(2):75-79. doi:10.1056/NEJM199501123320202
reports.followUp: Mean 2.8 years; planned follow-up three years

results.note: Intention to treat; composite included death, repeated or intractable retention, postvoid residual above 350 mL, bladder calculus, new persistent incontinence, high symptom score, or doubled creatinine. All tests were two-sided; P ≤ 0.05 was significant.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 76; Table 2 and Treatment Outcomes, p 77

results.endpoint: Symptoms, urinary bother, and daily activities
results.measure: Three-year symptom score (0–27), urinary-bother score and daily-activity score (both 0–100; higher is better), available follow-up assessments

effect.p: <0.001 for between-group changes in each measure

results.note: The greatest improvement in urinary bother after TURP was among men more bothered at baseline: 134/148 (91%) improved versus 45/73 (62%) of those less bothered.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Factors Influencing Outcomes, p 78

results.measure: Three-year urinary retention, high postvoid residual, and high symptom score, intention to treat
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Treatment Outcomes, p 77

results.measure: Three-year peak urinary flow and postvoid residual, available follow-up assessments

effect.p: <0.001 for flow change; 0.015 for residual-volume change

results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Change in Symptoms and Quality of Life, pp 77–78

harms.label: Persistent incontinence and sexual performance
harms.note: The three-year change in sexual-performance score was −3.0 after assignment to TURP and −3.2 after watchful waiting (P = 0.920); the 0–100 scale is higher for less impairment.
harms.locator: Full text, Tables 2–3 and Change in Symptoms and Quality of Life, pp 77–78

harms.label: Early postoperative complications
harms.value: Among 242 TURP procedures with complete operative information, repeat catheter placement occurred in 9/242 (3.7%), capsule perforation in 5/242 (2.1%), transfusion in 3/242 (1.2%), urinary infection in 2/242 (0.8%), and thrombophlebitis in 1/242 (0.4%) within 30 days; no surgery-associated deaths.

harms.label: Later corrective procedures after TURP
harms.value: Within three years after surgery, nine men underwent endoscopic surgery for bladder-neck contracture, nine needed urethral dilation for stricture, and eight had a second TURP (four for adenocarcinoma).

delivery.label: Early TURP receipt
delivery.value: 249/280 (88.9%) assigned to surgery underwent TURP within two weeks. Among 242 procedures with complete operative information, 97% were resected to the capsule; median tissue weight was 14 g (IQR 8–21 g), and 78% had a hospital stay of four days or less (mean 4 ± 4 days).
delivery.locator: Full text, Assignment to Treatment, p 75; Postoperative Events, pp 76–77

delivery.label: Watchful-waiting crossover
delivery.value: 65/276 (23.6%) assigned to watchful waiting underwent surgery within three years; 20 crossed over because of treatment failure.

delivery.label: Watchful-waiting regimen and follow-up
delivery.value: Both groups were advised to avoid coffee, alcohol, and other liquids after dinner and to avoid symptom-worsening medications; physicians were asked to avoid alpha-adrenergic antagonists. Visits occurred at six to eight weeks and then twice yearly for three years.
delivery.locator: Full text, Assignment to Treatment and Follow-up, pp 75–76

reports.label: Five-year follow-up
reports.citation: Flanigan RC, Reda DJ, Wasson JH, et al. "5-Year Outcome of Surgical Resection and Watchful Waiting for Men with Moderately Symptomatic Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: A Department of Veterans Affairs Cooperative Study." *J Urol.* 1998;160(1):12-17. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(01)63011-8
reports.followUp: Up to five years; mean 3.4 years (966 patient-years) for TURP and 3.6 years (990 patient-years) for watchful waiting

results.measure: Treatment failure through up to five years, intention to treat
results.note: Prespecified primary endpoint; all statistical tests were two-sided with 0.05 considered significant.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical methods and Table 1, p 13

results.measure: Urinary-retention component of treatment failure through up to five years, intention to treat
High-residual-volume component of treatment failure through up to five years, intention to treat

results.endpoint: Peak flow in men with low baseline flow
results.measure: Modeled change from baseline to 60 months at baseline peak flow 7 mL/s

values.ctl: +2.225 mL/s among men remaining on watchful waiting

effect.p: <0.0001 for initial TURP versus continued watchful waiting; 0.0002 versus later crossover

results.note: Men who crossed over from watchful waiting to TURP had modeled change +4.676 mL/s; as-treated groups were not randomized comparisons.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical methods, p 13, and Table 3, p 15

harms.label: Persistent incontinence
harms.note: Randomized-group comparison, P = 0.259; among men who actually underwent TURP, 3/250 (1.2%) had persistent incontinence.
harms.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 13, Table 2 and Discussion, p 14

harms.label: Repeat procedure after assignment to TURP

delivery.label: Watchful-waiting crossover at five years
delivery.value: 76/276 (27.5%) underwent TURP during observed follow-up; the five-year Kaplan–Meier cumulative crossover estimate was 36%.
